deep.reconstruction:
This page is a draft of Section 11, part II, of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (1854, published 1867). Its title is 'Darstellbarkeit by a trigonometric series whose terms do not tend to zero for every argument value.' The wording almost matches the printed text.

Setting (from the earlier part of the paper):
- Ω = A_0 + A_1 + A_2 + ..., with A_0 = b_0/2 and A_n = A_n(x) = a_n cos(nx) + b_n sin(nx).
- F(x) = C + C'x + A_0 x^2/2 - Σ_{n≥1} A_n(x)/n^2 is the twice formally integrated series.
- Part I treated the case a_n, b_n → 0. It proved, among other things, the localization theorem: μ^2 ∫_b^c F(t) cos μ(t-a) λ(t) dt → 0 as μ→∞. Here λ is the auxiliary function of the earlier sections: λ and λ' vanish at b and c, and λ'' has finitely many maxima and minima.

Step 1 (reduction). The case to treat is when the terms A_n(x) → 0 at the particular point x but not for every argument. Combine terms of equal rank in the series at x+t and x-t (my explicit step):
- A_n(x+t) + A_n(x-t) = 2 cos(nt) A_n(x), since cos n(x±t) and sin n(x±t) expand by the addition formulas.
- So Ω(x+t) + Ω(x-t) = 2A_0 + 2A_1 cos t + 2A_2 cos 2t + ...
- This is a cosine series in t whose coefficients A_n(x) tend to zero by hypothesis. So the theory of Part I applies to it as a function of t.

The page shows this paragraph twice: a first, heavily crossed-out attempt, then a clean restart.

Step 2 (the integrated function). Define G(t) = C + C'x + A_0 x^2/2 + A_0 t^2/2 - A_1 cos t/1 - A_2 cos 2t/4 - ... Check (mine):
- ((x+t)^2 + (x-t)^2)/2 = x^2 + t^2.
- Each term -A_n(x±t)/n^2 averages to -A_n(x) cos(nt)/n^2.
- Hence (F(x+t) + F(x-t))/2 = G(t) wherever the series for F(x+t) and F(x-t) converge. (They in fact always converge uniformly once the coefficients are bounded.)
- G is, up to constants, Riemann's F-function for the cosine series Σ A_n(x) cos(nt), whose coefficients tend to zero.

Step 3 (consequence I). If the terms of Ω tend to zero at x, then the localization theorem (Satz 3 of Part I) applied to G gives:
- μ^2 ∫_b^c G(t) cos μ(t-a) λ(t) dt → 0 as μ→∞, with λ as before.
- This integral splits into μ^2 ∫ F(x+t)/2 cos μ(t-a) λ(t) dt + μ^2 ∫ F(x-t)/2 cos μ(t-a) λ(t) dt, provided these have a meaning.

Step 4 (marginal remark, inserted). The vanishing cannot come about because each part tends to zero separately. Otherwise the terms of the series would tend to zero for every argument value (by the converse direction of Part I). Instead the contributions of points placed symmetrically on both sides of x must cancel each other. This is the germ of the printed remark that the behaviour of F at two symmetric places determines the result.
errors: In the second (clean) version the manuscript writes 'x+t und x+t' (or something ambiguous like x±t); it should read x+t and x-t. This is a slip of the pen.
The first attempt (repeated paragraph with the series 2A_0+2A_1 cos t+2A_2 cos 2t) is abandoned and redone. It is not an error, just draft duplication.

The phrase 'wofern diese Ausdrücke einen Sinn haben' correctly hedges the splitting of the integral. Since F is continuous when the coefficients are bounded, the split is in fact always legitimate. The justification of Step 4 (each part tending to zero would force A_n→0 everywhere) relies on Part I's converse theorems and is only asserted here, as in the published text.
No mathematical errors in the displayed formulas: the coefficient A_0 t^2/2, the factors 1/n^2, and the identity (F(x+t)+F(x-t))/2 = G(t) are all correct.

results.what: Symmetrization: A_n(x+t)+A_n(x-t)=2A_n(x)cos nt. This reduces the case 'terms →0 only at x' to a cosine series in t with coefficients →0.
results.modern_name: Symmetric (even) part of a trigonometric series about a point; reduction to cosine series

results.what: (F(x+t)+F(x-t))/2 = G(t), the Riemann function of the symmetrized series.
results.modern_name: Riemann function of the symmetrized series; symmetric second differences

results.what: Localization criterion applied to G: μ^2∫G(t)cosμ(t-a)λ(t)dt→0. The contributions at points symmetric about x must cancel, since they cannot vanish separately.
results.modern_name: Riemann localization principle (symmetric version) for series with coefficients not tending to zero

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of a passage of Riemann's own Habilitationsschrift (published posthumously by Dedekind in 1867). The text corresponds nearly verbatim to the printed §11 part II. Only minor draft variants are visible, such as the doubled opening and the marginal remark later reworded.

checkable.asserts: Cosine part of A_n(x+t)+A_n(x-t)=2A_n(x)cos nt (should be 0)
Sine part of the same identity (should be 0)
The quadratic term of (F(x+t)+F(x-t))/2 equals A0 x^2/2 + A0 t^2/2 (should be 0)
The n-th term of (F(x+t)+F(x-t))/2 equals -A_n(x)cos(nt)/n^2, the n-th term of G(t) (should be 0)
Second difference of -cos(nt)/n^2 with step 2α, divided by 4α^2, equals cos(nt)(sin nα/(nα))^2. This links G to the series ΣA_n cos nt (should be 0)

transcription_corrections: Title line: read 'deren Glieder nicht für jeden Argumentwerth zuletzt [unendlich] klein werden'. The machine version garbles the insertion.
Second version: the image has 'x+t und x+t' (a slip for x-t); the transcription silently corrected it to x-t.
'wie oben λ eine Function bezeichnet': the integrand is written G(t) cos μ(t-a) λ(t) dt. Earlier crossed-out 'λt dt' variants are visible.

The right-hand marginal block ('es ist aber zu bemerken, dass das Unendlichkleinwerden dieses Integrals hier nicht dadurch bewirkt werden kann, dass jeder Bestandtheil für sich immer unendlich klein wird ... sondern es müssen sich die [Beiträge der] symmetrisch zu beiden Seiten von x gelegenen Stellen einander aufheben') replaces the unfinished bottom-left sentence 'Es ist aber zu bemerken, dass hier nicht jeder dieser Bestandtheile für [sich] ...'.
